title: Ottawa Trivia Night

questions.q: Which Ottawa waterway, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, becomes a skateway in most winters?
Which monarch chose Ottawa as the capital in 1857?
Before it was renamed in 1855, what was Ottawa called?
Which Quebec city sits directly across the river from Parliament Hill?
What is the name of the clock tower at the centre of Parliament's Centre Block?
What is the name of Ottawa's CFL team?
Which country sends Ottawa tulip bulbs every year, in thanks for sheltering its royal family during the Second World War?
Which Ottawa-born singer had a 1957 hit with "Diana" and later wrote the English lyrics to "My Way"?
Lord Stanley donated hockey's Stanley Cup while living in Ottawa. What office did he hold?
What is the name of the winter festival, held every February in Ottawa and Gatineau, known for its ice sculptures?

notes: Rideau Canal; 2022-23 had no skating days, hence 'most winters'.
Queen Victoria selected Ottawa as capital of the Province of Canada on 31 December 1857; see Ottawa (Wikipedia) or Canadian Encyclopedia 'Ottawa'.
Bytown, named for Lt-Col John By, renamed Ottawa on incorporation as a city in 1855; see Canadian Encyclopedia 'Bytown'.
Gatineau, Quebec, faces Parliament Hill across the Ottawa River; see any map or Gatineau (Wikipedia).
The Peace Tower, the clock and bell tower of Centre Block, completed 1927; see Library of Parliament or parl.ca 'Peace Tower'.
Ottawa Redblacks, CFL team since 2014, Grey Cup champions 2016; see CFL.ca team page.
The Dutch royal family (Princess Juliana) sheltered in Ottawa during WWII; the Netherlands sends bulbs yearly, origin of the Canadian Tulip Festival. See tulipfestival.ca history.
Paul Anka, born Ottawa 30 July 1941; 'Diana' was a 1957 hit, and he wrote the English lyrics to 'My Way' (1969). See Paul Anka (Wikipedia).
Lord Stanley of Preston, Governor General 1888-1893, donated the Dominion Hockey Challenge Cup in 1892; see Hockey Hall of Fame (hhof.com) Stanley Cup history.
Winterlude (Bal de Neige), run by Canadian Heritage since 1979 across Ottawa and Gatineau each February; see canada.ca Winterlude pages or Winterlude (Wikipedia).
